items.title: Fire engulfs Jammu’s Nehru Market, guts around 12 shops
points: Fire breaks out at historic warehouse in Nehru market of Jammu city on November 8, 2026.

Picture: Screenshot from video posted on X/PTI_News Fire gutted at least a dozen shops in the historic Nehru Market in the heart of Jammu city on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, while a separate blaze broke out at the district police lines in Kathua…
A massive fire swept the Warehouse Nehru Market, one of Jammu's oldest wholesale hubs of food grains, essential commodities and other daily-use items.
The Fire and Emergency Services Department said the fire began in one of the shops at around 9.15 p.m. and spread quickly to adjoining establishments due to storage of edible oil.
At the site, Divisional Commissioner, Jammu, Vikas Kundal, said the fire had been largely brought under control.
"What started as a small fire has engulfed around 15 shops and threatens to spread further.
BJP MLA Vikram Randhawa said at least eight shops were gutted in fire.

Delhi-NCR Chokes On Diwali Night As Smoke Engulfs City, AQI Nears 400
points: As the nation celebrates Diwali, a thick blanket of smoke has engulfed the Delhi-NCR region.
In the run-up to Diwali, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) enforced Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR.
As per data provided by the CPCB on the Sameer app, the overall AQI of Delhi as of 11:05 PM on November 8, 2026, stood at 373 in the “very poor” category.
The average AQI of Noida, at the same time, was recorded at 319 in the “very poor” category, while the AQI at Ghaziabad, Gurugram, and Faridabad stood at 360, 280, and 297, respectively.
Several areas in the national capital like Alipur, Bawana, Burari, Chandni Chowk, Mundka, Punjabi Bagh, Rohini, and Vivek Vihar, among others, recorded an AQI above 400 in the “severe” category.
This data comes as notifications by the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) for Delhi predicted that air quality is likely to remain in the 'severe' category from November 9 for a few days.

Thick smog blankets Delhi on Deepavali night, AQI at 20 stations ‘severe’
points: The city’s air quality remained in the very poor category, with the instantaneous Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 371 at 7 p.m., close to the severe threshold.
Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.
The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..
Similar reports came from Mayur Vihar, while people in the Bishambardas Marg area and Lutyens’ Delhi said fireworks continued, although the intensity had reduced slightly.
Of the 59 monitoring stations, 19 were in the 'severe' category at 7 p.m., seven in the 'poor' category, and the remaining 33 in the 'very poor' category.
The city's average AQI for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category, compared to 369 on Saturday, amid a layer of smog and reduced visibility.
